- spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity
- extraction artifacts = document-noise
- genuinely different company or person names = different-entity

"HBM Hottinger Baldwin Messtechnik GmbH" vs "Hottinger Baldwin Messtechnik GmbH" — the core legal name is identical; "HBM" is the well-known brand name/abbreviation of the same company (HBM is literally the initials of Hottinger Baldwin Messtechnik... actually HBM stands for Hottinger Baldwin Messtechnik). This is the same entity. The document adds the brand prefix, which doesn't create a different company.

Is it "same-entity" with best_value being...? For same-entity, which best value? For company names with spelling drift, presumably canonical register form is fine, but the document is the legal instrument. Hmm. The rules explicitly say for different-entity, best_value = document's. For same-entity, only the number/year case says register's canonical form. But generally, for a fused record, the fuller legal name from the certificate could be preferred since the certificate is the legal instrument. However, "HBM Hottinger Baldwin Messtechnik GmbH" — is that actually the legal name? The actual company was "Hottinger Baldwin Messtechnik GmbH", trading as HBM. The certificate document says "HBM Hottinger Baldwin Messtechnik GmbH" per the extraction. The document is the legal instrument, so best_value could be the document's fuller name.

The verdict is "same-entity". Actually, a fused record should probably keep the register's canonical form or the document's? The rules only mandate register canonical form for certificate number/year formats. For names, no explicit rule, but "the certificate is the legal instrument" principle suggests document value when they differ meaningfully. Since the document's value is a superset (identical legal name + brand), carrying the document's value loses no information. I'll pick the document's value.

Why: "HBM" is the brand acronym of the same legal name; identical core entity.
